product_brief: A general-purpose hybrid post-quantum/traditional key encapsulation mechanism (KEM) built on X25519 and ML-KEM-768.
pqc_capability_description: Implements X-Wing, a hybrid KEM combining X25519 (traditional) and ML-KEM-768 (post-quantum, FIPS 203). It is defined in Internet-Draft draft-connolly-cfrg-xwing-kem-10. Implementations exist in Apple CryptoKit, Google's BoringSSL, Cloudflare's CIRCL, and Rust libraries.
primary_platforms: Apple CryptoKit, Google's BoringSSL, Cloudflare's CIRCL (Go), Rust (xwing-kem.rs, RustCrypto, Orion)
implementation_attack_surface: The reference Python specification is not production-ready, is slow, does not run in constant time, and leaks the private key by its runtime.
testing_&_validation_methods: Test vectors provided in Appendix C; deterministic test vector generation supported via derandomized key generation and encapsulation.

product_brief: A toolkit providing cryptographic functions and security features, including support for TLS, PKCS, and various cryptographic algorithms.
pqc_capability_description: Added LMS signature verification support as per SP 800-208. This support is present in both the FIPS and default providers.
crypto_primitives: LMS, ECDSA, RSA, AES-OCB, AES-GCM-SIV, AES-SIV, AES-CFB-128, FFC-DH, PBMAC1
fips_validated: Yes (FIPS provider mentioned; LMS support present in FIPS provider; FIPS 186-5 deterministic ECDSA support added to FIPS provider)
primary_platforms: Unknown (VxWorks support removed; requires C-99 compilers)
implementation_attack_surface: Memory safety issues including heap use-after-free, double-free, NULL pointer dereference, heap buffer overflow, out-of-bounds read/write, and Bleichenbacher Oracle vulnerabilities.

product_brief: A benchmarking project for Korean Post-Quantum Cryptography (KpqC) algorithms, inspired by PQClean.
pqc_capability_description: Provides performance benchmarks and memory/constant-time analysis for KpqC competition algorithms. Includes Lattice-based (NTRUplus, SMAUG, TiGER, GCKSign, HAETAE, NCCSign, Peregrine, SOLMAE), Code-based (PALOMA, IPCC, Layered-ROLLO, Enhanced pqsigRM), Zero-knowledge (AIMer), and Multivariate Quadratic (MQSign) schemes.
crypto_primitives: NTRUplus, PALOMA, SMAUG, TiGER, REDOG, Layered-ROLLO, IPCC, AIMer, GCKSign, HAETAE, MQSign, NCCSign, Peregrine, SOLMAE, Enhanced pqsigRM, FIBS
signature_schemes: AIMer, GCKSign, HAETAE, MQSign, NCCSign, Peregrine, SOLMAE, Enhanced pqsigRM, FIBS
implementation_attack_surface: Memory leaks found in three algorithms (unspecified which). Constant-time risks identified: GCKSign (L2 risk in poly_reject_z); AIMer, HAETAE, NCCSign, Enhanced pqsigRM, IPCC, Layered ROLLO-I, SMAUG, TiGER, PALOMA have L3 risks or uninitialized variable issues. REDOG and FIBS could not be tested.
testing_&_validation_methods: Benchmarking using 'rdtsc' instruction; Memory consumption analysis using Valgrind massif; Memory leak detection using Valgrind; Constant-time implementation verification using Valgrind logs.
constrained_device_&_iot_suitability: Tested on Raspberry Pi (ARMv7l, 1.4GHz, 1GB RAM) with specific iteration counts and nano-second units.
